items.title: State notification channel payload slimmed to a pointer
items.description: The platform-managed 'state' notification channel (NotificationTask state channel and the new state-level notification directive) no longer embeds the full State function output (GetInstanceStateOutput) in the message data. The data payload is now the slim pointer { domain, flow, id, version } inside the CloudEvents envelope; consumers must re-fetch the full state via the State function. Binding metadata and IStateNotificationMapping enrichment are unchanged.
items.action: Update state-channel consumers to treat the message as a change pointer and call the State function for full state instead of reading data.data.* fields.

items.title: Schema x-roles DENY now applies across the whole grant set
items.description: Field-level visibility used to evaluate each caller role against a path's grants in isolation, and a path was visible if any single role passed. A DENY naming a predefined role was therefore defeated whenever the caller also held some unrelated role: that role matched nothing, the deny-only set fell through to the blacklist rule, and the field stayed visible. Evaluation now runs the canonical rule over the whole grant set, so a matching DENY hides the field regardless of the caller's other roles. Fields previously exposed by this gap become hidden.
items.action: Review every schema declaring a DENY in x-roles. If a field was relied upon as visible while a DENY grant matched the caller, the declaration was not expressing that — replace the DENY with an explicit ALLOW list for the roles that should see the field.

items.title: Schema x-roles: a role-less caller now sees deny-only fields
items.description: A caller with no roles was rejected before the grant rule was applied, so a path guarded only by DENY grants was hidden from them. The canonical blacklist rule now applies: a grant set with no ALLOW grant allows anyone it does not explicitly deny, including a role-less caller. Note that a path guarded by an ALLOW grant is still hidden from a role-less caller, so allowlist declarations are unaffected.
items.action: If a field must never reach an unauthenticated or role-less caller, declare it with an explicit ALLOW list instead of relying on DENY grants alone.

items.title: Human-task list authorization now matches the transition-execution rule
items.description: The list split a transition's grants into static and predefined subsets, evaluated each separately and required BOTH to match. A transition declaring [allow: teller, allow: $InstanceStarter] was therefore only listed for a caller who was both a teller and the instance starter, even though either one alone was enough to execute it — the task was hidden from users who could act on it. The list now applies the same any-matching-ALLOW rule as execution and additionally honors dynamic $.context.* grants, which it previously ignored entirely. Expect more tasks to appear for the same caller.
items.action: Re-check human-task expectations for transitions that mix static and predefined grants. To require both conditions, model the second as a DENY for the complement rather than relying on the old AND behavior.

items.title: updateData no longer re-runs the state's OnEntry/OnExit or re-arms its timers
items.description: updateData previously ran the full pipeline: the current state's OnExit tasks ran, its OnEntry tasks ran a second time, and the state's scheduled transitions were cancelled and re-armed - restarting every timeout from zero. Those four steps (CancelScheduledJobs, OnExit, OnEntry, Schedule) are now excluded for updateData, whose target is fixed to the reserved $self key and which therefore leaves and enters no state. The transition's own onExecute tasks, the data write and the auto-transition evaluation are unchanged. This applies to updateData ONLY. Other transitions declaring target $self - shared transitions in particular - are unaffected and keep running the full state lifecycle, as do transitions naming the current state literally, including self-loops.
items.action: If a workflow relied on updateData re-running the current state's OnEntry to refresh something, move that logic into the transition's own onExecutionTasks. If it relied on updateData resetting the state's scheduled-transition timer, model the reset explicitly. Only the workflow-level updateData transition is affected, so no search of state transitions is needed. Note the converse for $self shared transitions, which are unchanged: because they still cancel and re-arm the state's scheduled transitions, a frequently invoked one on a state with a short timeout defers that timeout on every call.

items.title: Script metrics: cache hit/miss split and true execution metrics added
items.description: New metrics: script_compilations_total{result=hit|miss,status}; script_execution_duration_seconds{script_type,language,status} and script_runtime_errors_total{script_type,language,error_type} are now recorded at execution funnels (task-input, task-output, condition, transition-mapping, function); script_compilation_duration_seconds gained a 'cache' label (existing aggregate queries unaffected); workflow_cache_entries gained cache_name='script-types'. script_executions_total is deprecated but unchanged.
items.action: Point compile-rate panels at rate(script_compilations_total[5m]); read clean compile latency with {cache="miss"}; use script_execution_duration_seconds_count for true execution counts. No urgent action: old metric still emits.

items.title: Task audit request now stores a task reference instead of the full definition
items.description: InstanceTask.Request previously embedded the entire task definition (including mapping script code) on every execution. It now stores { key, version, domain, flow, type }; the definition lives in the component store. InputResponse is unchanged. Monitoring passes Request through as raw JSON, so no monitor field parsing is affected.
items.action: If any external consumer parsed request.task.* definition fields (e.g. config, mapping code), resolve the definition from the component store by the embedded reference instead.

items.title: Instance data reads share one materialized tree per data version
items.description: context.Instance.Data previously materialized a fresh dynamic tree on EVERY access, so script-side mutations of it were silently lost. Reads are now memoized per data version: a mutation becomes visible to subsequent reads within the same transition (it is still NEVER persisted — persistence remains delta-only via ScriptResponse.Data). Similarly, parallel-branch task response VALUES are now shared by reference between parent and branch (containers stay isolated); in-place mutation of a pre-existing response value inside a branch is visible to the parent after join.
items.action: Scripts must not mutate context.Instance.Data or pre-existing task response values in place and rely on the old silent-discard; return deltas via ScriptResponse.Data as documented.

items.title: SetBody preserves ExpandoObject/list keys as authored instead of camelCasing them
items.description: SetBody (and the WithBody builder path) with an ExpandoObject/List input now clones structurally and PRESERVES dictionary keys as authored; previously such input was serialized with the global options whose DictionaryKeyPolicy camelCased keys. Anonymous-object/POCO inputs still camelCase (unchanged). This aligns SetBody with SetStandardResponse (which never camelCased dict keys) and with instance-data trees (camelCase at persist).
items.action: Scripts relying on SetBody camelCasing PascalCase expando keys must camelCase their own keys.

items.title: Parallel-branch merge conflict detection is now structural and order-insensitive
items.description: Parallel-branch merge conflict detection now compares JsonElement values structurally (JsonElement.DeepEquals — object property order ignored); previously the comparison was serialized-text based and order-sensitive, so reordered-but-structurally-equal outputs threw a false conflict. Same-content different-order now merges.
items.action: None expected; conflict semantics for genuinely different content unchanged.

items.title: Self-referencing script values now fail fast instead of being silently truncated
items.description: Body/branch cloning moved from a JSON round-trip to a structural clone. The old round-trip used ReferenceHandler.IgnoreCycles, so a script that assigned an ExpandoObject into itself (directly or transitively) had the repeated reference silently replaced with null and the task continued with truncated data. The structural clone instead detects the runaway nesting and throws InvalidOperationException at depth 256, so the task fails visibly through the normal error boundary rather than persisting quietly corrupted content. Acyclic values — every value that originates from JSON — are unaffected.
items.action: Scripts must not build self-referencing dynamic values. If a mapping legitimately nests deeper than 256 levels, flatten it; if a task starts failing with this message, inspect the mapping for a value assigned into itself instead of into a delta.

items.title: Incidents live in their own table; read surfaces carry links, not incident content
items.description: InstanceIncident rows moved from the Instances.Incidents jsonb array (pruned to the newest 5) to the InstanceIncidents table with unbounded history, backfilled by the BackfillInstanceIncidents migration; the stored generated HasActiveIncident column became a real column maintained by the runtime. Consequences on read surfaces: metadata.incident on GET .../instances/{instance} and on every list item now carries LINKS rather than content — { hasActiveIncident, active: { href }, history: { href } }, with active present only while an incident is open — which is byte-for-byte the state function's incident block, so clients learn one shape. The embedded active incident, the inline newest-5 history array, the totalCount field and the flat href are all GONE; fetch the detail through active.href (GET .../incidents/active, 404 Instance:100037 when nothing is open) or page history.href. scripts' context.Incident.TotalIncidentCount counts the incidents materialized on the instance (the unresolved ones plus those recorded in the current transition), not the full persisted history, and context.Incident.IncidentsLoaded was added. The legacy jsonb column stays in the database (unmapped) for this release and is dropped by a later release's migration. DbMigrator now honors SchemaMigration:CommandTimeoutSeconds (default 600) and SchemaMigration:LockExpirySeconds (default 900), and exits non-zero when any schema fails to migrate.
items.action: Read the active incident from GET .../instances/{instance}/incidents/active and the history from GET .../instances/{instance}/incidents (or the Monitor endpoint) instead of expecting either inline: metadata.incident and the state function's incident block carry links only. Treat a 404 from the active endpoint as 'no incident open, re-read the state', not as an error. Do not read metadata.incident.active/history/totalCount/href — those fields no longer exist; do not query the Instances.Incidents jsonb column directly — it is frozen at its pre-migration content and will be removed. If a schema migration needs longer than 600 s per statement, raise SchemaMigration:CommandTimeoutSeconds (and LockExpirySeconds above it) for the DbMigrator job.

items.title: One incident per failure; a re-faulting retry stays faulted; unfault closes every open incident
items.description: Three defects on the incident/retry path were corrected in the same release that moved incidents to their own table. (a) An abort — or an unhandled task failure with no matching boundary rule — used to record TWO incidents: the boundary's own verdict plus a pipeline-layer row (errorCode "ErrorBoundaryAbort", errorLayer "Pipeline", no task attribution) that, being newer, became metadata.incident.active and the state body's incident.active. The three task steps now record the incident before their own save, so the row and the HasActiveIncident flag commit together and the pipeline's fault path skips its fallback row: one failure leaves exactly one incident and active is the boundary's verdict, carrying boundaryAction whenever a rule resolved one. A side effect on rollback/notify outcomes is a brief hasActiveIncident=true window on the Busy instance before FinalizeTransitionStep closes the row; the committed end state is unchanged. (b) POST .../instances/{instance}/retry whose re-executed work faulted again answered 200 with "status":"F" and then settled the instance back to Active, because the aggregate was loaded tracked in the ambient request unit of work and the ambient commit overwrote the Faulted an inner scope had persisted. The instance was left looking healthy, unfinished, and permanently unretryable (400 Instance:100027). Retry now reads no-tracking and unfaults with a compare-and-set, so the response status is durable and a second retry is accepted. (c) A successful retry resolved only the newest incident, so a recovered instance kept reporting hasActiveIncident=true — and because that flag is state-function ETag material, long-polling clients saw the stale signal too. Unfault, and a boundary transition that completes without a new fault, now resolve every open incident on the instance and recompute the flag. History rows are kept and marked resolved. Unchanged and still true: incident.retryCount is always 0 (the resolved retry policy is not attached to the action result), and ignore/log record no incident and skip the remainder of the hook. These three fixes changed values rather than the response shape; the shape itself was replaced separately in the same release, taking ResponseShapeVersion to v9 — see instance-incidents-moved-to-separate-table. Instances that already carry two rows, or a stale flag, are not repaired retroactively; they stay as they are until their next unfault.
items.action: Do not key off the incident's errorCode "ErrorBoundaryAbort" (the pipeline no longer writes that row; the same string is still the Result error code an aborting boundary returns) or expect two incidents per failure — read the single incident's boundaryAction/boundaryLevel instead, and treat their absence as "no rule matched". Treat a retry response's "status":"F" as the persisted status and retry again if appropriate; drop any workaround that treated an F response followed by an Active instance as terminal. Read hasActiveIncident as authoritative after recovery rather than filtering resolved incidents client-side. If you need the attempt count, write it from the task's own mapping into instance data — retryCount still reports 0.

items.title: Sync start and transition responses no longer evaluate extensions
items.description: A sync=true start or transition used to run the workflow's Extensions while projecting its response and return them under `extensions`. It no longer does: extensions are enrichment, not data. The client workflow manager never read them off a write response, and a service-to-service caller already receives `attributes`. The `extensions` key is KEPT on the response and is always an empty object, so the response shape is unchanged. Extensions still run unchanged on every READ surface — GET instance, GET instances, the data function (GET .../functions/data?extensions=) and the extensions endpoint — so anything that needs an extension value asks for it there. Two side effects: the `?extensions=` query parameter was removed from the start and transition endpoints (it is a no-op parameter now, and an old caller that still sends it is not rejected), and the response projection no longer builds a ScriptContext for a workflow without an output mapping, because extensions were its only other consumer.
items.action: Move any client that read `extensions` off a sync start/transition response to a read surface — GET .../instances/{instance}/functions/data?extensions=<key>, the instance GET or the instance list — and drop `?extensions=` from start and transition calls (it is no longer bound; sending it is harmless). Expect `"extensions": {}` on every sync start/transition response: the key stays so the shape does not change, the content never fills.

items.title: Instance filter scalar operands longer than 1000 characters are now rejected
items.description: BREAKING CHANGE: MaxValueLength previously existed without enforcement on instance filters, so an operand longer than 1000 characters could succeed while the full filter remained within 5000 characters. HTTP queries now return 400 with filter.valueTooLong before SQL execution. GetInstancesTask validates before both local and remote dispatch; invalid operands fail the task and can trigger its workflow error boundary, potentially faulting the instance depending on boundary rules. The limit is inclusive and counts decoded UTF-16 code units (.NET string.Length). Arrays and legacy comma-separated in/nin/between operands are checked per element, not by combined length. Includes keeps its separate object-payload limits; stored instance data is not truncated and the overall filter-string limit is unchanged.
items.action: Before upgrading, audit client-generated filters, authored GetInstancesTask filters and mapping-generated operands. Replace oversized query operands with suitable short lookup keys or revise the query contract; do not blindly truncate values and change matching semantics. Verify workflow boundary handling for filter.valueTooLong. There is no configuration switch to relax this limit.

items.title: x-indexed metadata is validated against attributes.type master
items.description: Schema publication, including schema seed items, rejects any x-indexed metadata outside a component whose attributes.type is exactly master, even when the annotation is false. A true annotation additionally requires an explicit supported scalar property path. Other attributes.type values remain valid without x-indexed; JSON Schema type keywords inside attributes.schema do not declare the component a Master, and there is no new root type field. Declaring x-indexed does not create indexes.
items.action: Remove x-indexed from non-master schema components; use attributes.type=master only for actual Master schemas. Keep true annotations on supported scalar properties and retain x-filterOperators/x-sortable permissions. Use compatible vnext-schema and vnext-workflow-cli releases for authoring validation and offline SQL generation. Have the DBA review and execute generated SQL before enabling AttributeIndexes:Enabled; do not rely on sync/update or host startup to run DDL.

items.title: A component deployment must signal publish-completed once at the end
items.description: definitions/re-initialize is removed and definitions/publish/completed takes its place. The call is made once, after the last component of a package has been published, and its body reports what each post-deployment hook did. The hook that ships today forces a re-read of the domain discovery registry, which - because the discovery endpoint cache no longer has a TTL - is that cache's only automatic invalidation. A pipeline that never makes the call leaves the runtime resolving cross-domain calls by whatever it learned at startup until the pod restarts, and both old callers swallow the 404 from the removed endpoint without failing, so nothing surfaces the omission.
items.action: Upgrade vnext-workflow-cli to a release that calls publish/completed (wf sync / update / reset do it automatically) and release it before or together with the runtime. A pipeline that posts components to definitions/publish directly must add one call to POST /api/v1/definitions/publish/completed at the end and gate on the response body's success field, not on the status code, which is always 200. The init host's package endpoints already do this unconditionally; its former reInitialize request flag is gone and is ignored if sent.

items.title: Duplicate function task keys are rejected at publish
items.description: Component validation now refuses a function whose onExecutionTasks contain two entries whose task keys resolve to the same response variable name (ToVariableName normalization: 'user-info' and 'user_info' both become 'userInfo'). Each task files its result under that variable in ScriptContext.TaskResponse/OutputResponse, so colliding keys silently overwrote each other's slot and the output script read one task's payload where it expected the other's. Previously such definitions published without complaint; a republish or update of an existing definition with colliding keys now fails validation with the member Function.OnExecutionTasks[i].
items.action: Rename the colliding task keys so each normalizes to a distinct variable name (and update the output script's TaskResponse/OutputResponse reads to match) before republishing the function.

items.title: Async transition job payloads are reference-only
items.description: An async (sync=false) accept whose request body exceeds WorkflowExecution:AsyncTransitionInlineBodyMaxBytes (1 MiB default) persists the body in the new InstanceJobRequestData table; the Dapr job payload and the TransitionContinuationRequested outbox event carry DataInJobRow + the JobId instead of the body, keeping every message under the scheduler's (etcd) and pub/sub's ceilings. Smaller bodies stay inline unchanged. The job handler hydrates an offloaded body back from the table; in-flight payloads from older builds that carry Data inline keep working. A deferred-arm failure after the accept's commit falls back to the transactional outbox (durable re-arm, instance stays Busy) instead of leaving it stuck.
items.action: No authoring change. Operators: drain async transition jobs before rolling the runtime back past the AddInstanceJobRequestDataTable migration, and prefer draining during a forward rolling deploy too — a pod without this change runs an offloaded (DataInJobRow) job with an empty body. Keep AsyncTransitionInlineBodyMaxBytes high enough that ordinary transitions stay inline and are unaffected by the mixed-version window.
